public_health_question.v: How available and promoted are lower-sodium food options in stores and restaurants in Guam?

ev.q: To determine the availability and promotion of lower-sodium options in the nutrition environment
conducted an assessment in September 2015 using previously validated tools adapted to include sodium measures
Assessments used the previously validated Nutrition Environment Measures Surveys for stores and for restaurants
Assessments used the previously validated Nutrition Environment Measures Surveys for stores and for restaurants
Sodium in Store and Restaurant Food Environments — Guam, 2015

equity.level_reason: Units are stores and restaurants compared by size and type; no social-position dimension is analyzed. Language barriers appear only as a limitation on manager participation.

level_alternative.reason: Non-English-speaking managers are named in a limitation, which could be read as equity raised only as a limitation.

ev.q: non-English speaking managers might have been less likely to participate, although translators were used when possible.

equity.equity_measurement: Sampling by region (north, central, south) is geography, not an SPD; SNAP listings used only to build the sampling frame.

notes: Design is called an 'assessment'; mapped to cross-sectional. No health condition is measured; the outcomes are food-environment availability, price and promotion, so conditions is empty (CVD and sodium intake are context). Manager questionnaire percentages are unweighted descriptive results from a convenience sample.
view_issues: Text says 3% of restaurants identified lower-sodium items in one place, but Table 3 gives 0.8% and the abstract 1%; the 3% figure appears to be for sodium information posting. Table 1 note marks hot dogs without † though text lists it among <50%.
